  • 実行中フレームを持つ無効化（BOP、側方退出）は、コードではなくフレームを 書き換えることで解決する。返りアドレスの差し替えが chain deopt の核心。
  • TracePoint の不在は暗黙の不変条件であり、実装するなら BOP と同型の グローバル無効化として設計するのが自然。
  • 非移動 GC も暗黙の不変条件である。

Invalidating compiled code — and repairing it instead

Compiled code bakes in answers that Ruby is allowed to change later: which FuncId a call site dispatches to, what value a folded constant has, which operator is still the builtin. monoruby guards those answers with two global version counters, and a guard failure used to mean one thing — throw the body away and compile it again.

That was far too blunt. The counters are global: any def anywhere moves the class version, any X = 1 anywhere moves the constant version. A program that keeps defining things (a spec suite, a Rails boot) moved them constantly, so hot bodies were recompiled over and over even though nothing they had cached had actually changed.

Salvage is the answer: on a guard failure, re-validate what the body assumed. If every assumption still holds, stamp the current version into the body and keep the code. Only a genuine change recompiles. On a ruby/spec core run this turns ~107,000 recompiles into ~320.

This document covers what moves the counters, how a unit records what it assumed, and how each guard failure is repaired. For the stub and class-guard-chain shapes the guards live in, see jit.md; for basic-operator redefinition — the one invalidation that is not repaired this way — see bop_redefinition.md.

1. The two counters, and what moves them

Both live in Codegen (codegen.rs) and are read by compiled code as a plain memory word.

Class version — Globals::class_version_inc():

SiteTrigger
Store::insert_method (globals/store/class.rs)def, define_method, attr_*, alias_method
Store::remove_methodremove_method, undef_method
visibility update (same file)public / private / protected on an existing entry
include_or_prepend_module (value/rvalue/module.rs)include, prepend
refinement import (builtins/module.rs), using (executor.rs)refine, using — see refinements.md §6.1

Constant version — Globals::const_version_inc(), and the per-name epochs described in §4:

SiteTriggerEpoch bumped
Globals::set_constantany constant assignment, including the firstthat name
Globals::remove_constantremove_constthat name
bare const_version_inc() (value/rvalue/module.rs)include / prepend — resolution may change without any assignmentwildcard

Note the third row: an event with no single name to attribute the change to bumps a wildcard epoch, which makes every unit’s fast path (§4) conservative until it re-validates.

extend on an object that had no singleton class moves neither. Module#extend_object (builtins/module.rs) makes the singleton class and includes the module into it in one call, and nothing can have resolved a method or a constant through a class that did not exist when the call began (ClassIds are never reused, so “its id is at or above the table length read before get_singleton” is exact). That include goes through Module::include_module_into_new_singleton, which skips both increments. The object leaving its old class is the business of the latch in singleton_class_facts.md, exactly as for obj.singleton_class, which never moved a version. An object that already has a singleton class, and any class or module, take the ordinary include path. This is what a program that decorates every object it builds needs: Loofah extends each node of the documents it scrubs, about 300 a request in shipit, and each one used to fail every unit’s class guard and const guard (87,500 class-guard salvages and 41,600 const-guard recoveries per request).

2. One patchable snapshot word per compilation unit

A compilation unit is a root body plus every specialized callee inlined into it. jit_compile (codegen/jitgen.rs) creates one class-version word and — when the body folded at least one constant — one const-version word for the whole unit:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
let class_version_label = self.jit.const_i32(class_version as _);
let const_version_label = (!const_folds.is_empty())
    .then(|| self.jit.const_i64(const_version as _));
}

Every guard in the unit, children included, compares the global counter against that one word. Compilation is atomic at one version, so one word is enough — and one store re-validates the entire unit. set_class_version / set_const_version (codegen.rs) are that store.

The snapshot’s representation differs per arch. aarch64 reads the word (a64_guard_class_version takes the unit’s label). x86-64 bakes the snapshot into each guard as a patchable imm32 — a fixed 5-byte movl rax, imm32 whose last 4 bytes salvage re-stamps — removing the per-unit data load (one scattered cache line per compilation unit, ~1 D1 miss per call in call-dense code) from the hot path. This is safe only because every imm site is registered: check_version (arch/x86_64/guard.rs) is the single emitter of the compare and pushes its patch label into unit_version_patch_sites; jit_compile files the unit’s list under its snapshot-word address (version_imm_sites), and set_class_version patches the word and every registered site. The word itself is retained as the salvage records’ key (and as what aarch64 reads), so the record plumbing is unchanged.

The history that makes the registration invariant load-bearing: aarch64 once baked the snapshot as an unpatched immediate, which silently made salvage a no-op there — the word was patched and the guard kept comparing against the old immediate (fixed in #1157). An immediate is acceptable exactly when its patch site cannot be forgotten; a guard shape that emits its own compare instead of going through check_version would reintroduce the bug.

The word is reachable afterwards through the unit’s salvage record:

Unit kindRecordKeyed by
whole methodISeqInfo::jit_entry → JitInfoself_class
loop (OSR)ISeqInfo::loop_jit_info → LoopJitInfo(self_class, LoopStart index)
specialized childits owner’s record, via SpecializedPatchEntry::owner—

3. Class-version salvage

JitInfo / LoopJitInfo carry an inline_cache_map: Vec<InlineCacheEntry> — every method call the compiler resolved at compile time, as (recv_class, name, refinements, func_id). Store::salvage_method_unit / salvage_loop_unit (globals/store/class.rs) re-ask each question with check_method_for_name and compare the answer:

  • all unchanged → return the unit’s version label; the caller patches it and the code stands.
  • any changed → None; recompile.

A unit that carried a class proof across a call also records the classes it assumed have no instance with a singleton class (singleton_deps); salvage refuses once one has — see singleton_class_facts.md.

Two details that are easy to get wrong:

  • The refinement set is part of the question. Re-asking the unrefined question after a using moved the version would confirm an answer the code is no longer allowed to give (refinements.md §3.4).
  • super sites are re-asked about the body they were compiled for. A super entry (name: None) carries super_of, the method body the compiler resolved the super against (jit_check_super’s mother — the site’s own iseq’s, which for a specialized callee is not the unit’s root), and the salvage asks check_super(class, super_of, name) again. That needs no frame because the JIT compiles only frame-independent super sites: not a define_method body (its super follows the called name) and not a body that occupies several positions in the ancestry (compile/method_call.rs deopts both). The method-name index files the entry under that body’s name. Before this the salvage needed the executing frame and failed without it, so every unit with a specialized initialize that calls super (Class#new inlining one) recompiled on every class-version move: shipit, whose Loofah extends each node it scrubs, filled the 1 GiB code page that way.

Specialized children salvage their owner. A child’s guard reads the owner’s word, and the owner’s cache map covers the child’s call sites, so salvage_specialized (codegen/compiler.rs) validates the owner unit. SpecializedPatchEntry::owner is cleared to None when a child is recompiled individually: the fresh body reads its own fresh words, which the owner’s record no longer names, and patching the owner’s word would “heal” words that body never reads — deopting it on every call, forever.

4. Const-version salvage — two tiers

A const-version guard failure says only “some constant event happened somewhere”. ConstSalvageMap (globals/store/iseq.rs) records what the unit actually folded — for each site, the ConstCache tuple the emitted code relies on and the names whose redefinition could change its resolution (the final name plus every path qualifier) — plus a snapshot of those names’ epochs at compile time.

Store::salvage_const_unit then escalates:

  1. Per-name epochs. Every event in §1 bumps the epoch of the name it touched. If no folded name’s epoch moved (and the wildcard didn’t), no fold can have changed — patch the word, done, without a single lookup. This is the common case: a spec file defining unrelated constants.
  2. Value re-check. For a site whose name was touched, compare the fold against that site’s VM inline cache. A cache already refreshed at the current version whose (value, base_class, self_class) equals the fold proves the assignment wrote the same value — patch and keep. A differing value recompiles. A stale cache (the VM has not re-run the site at this version yet) returns ConstSalvage::Defer: skip the recompile, let this invocation deopt so the interpreter refreshes the cache, and retry on the next miss. Bounded by stale_defers (3) so a fold whose site the deopted execution never reaches cannot defer forever.

The recorded fold values are GC roots: ConstSalvageMap::mark is reached from ISeqInfo::mark, so a folded Value stays alive as long as the code that baked it in.

5. Where a guard miss goes

All misses call into Rust before deciding. The entry points live in codegen/compiler.rs.

Unitx86-64aarch64
whole method, class verjit_recompile_method_with_recovery — on a successful salvage returns 1 and the stub’s jnz recover resumes in place, no deoptjit_recompile_method — salvages, then deopts once
whole method, const verjit_recompile_method → salvage_method_constsame
loop (OSR)jit_recompile_loop → salvage_loop (class or const)same
specializedjit_recompile_specialized → salvage_specializedsame

Except for x86’s resume-in-place path, a successful salvage still lets the current invocation deopt to the VM once; the healed code passes its guards from the next call or iteration.

Salvage must run outside the CODEGEN borrow. Validation reads Globals::class_version() / const_version(), which borrow the same thread-local RefCell — so the salvage attempt sits in the extern "C" entry point, before CODEGEN.with(...), and the helpers in Store return the DestLabel for the caller to patch in its own borrow context rather than patching it themselves.

Const guards are not counter-gated. The generic recompile side exit (SideExit::RecompileDeoptimize → AsmInst::RecompileDeopt, gated by COUNT_DEOPT_RECOMPILE) is one-shot: once drained it never re-arms. That is right for an expensive recompile but wrong for a cheap salvage — the second version move after a successful salvage would strand the body in the interpreter for the rest of the run. So a const-version miss calls the salvaging entry on every failure, the same shape the class-version guard uses. A block-style root is the exception and keeps a plain deopt: the whole-method recompile entry rebuilds whatever lfp.func_id() names as a method, which is the wrong frame shape for a block body.

6. What is not salvaged

ReasonBehaviour
NotCached, MethodNotFound, IvarIdNotFoundthe compiler lacked information; recompiling with a warmed VM cache is the point
BecamePolymorphica monomorphic-compiled send saw a second class. Ratcheted: recompile while the PMC holds fewer than two classes, plain deopt afterwards (RecvMissMode::Learn)
basic-operator redefinitionnot a version guard. Bodies that inlined the operator are evicted (ISeqInfo::evict_jit_code, bop_deps) — see bop_redefinition.md
front-end baila whole-method bail marks the iseq jit_invalidated, and it is never compiled again; a loop bail just leaves the site interpreted

7. The megamorphic gate

Salvage repairs code that is still correct. The complementary question — should this receiver class be compiled at all? — is answered by the class-guard chain’s miss exit, and it is worth stating because getting it wrong is invisible.

A chain miss must leave the chain and run the call in the interpreter (jit_class_guard_fail: jmp vm_entry). The stub samples the receiver class only when its warm-up counter expires, so a class used for a single call is sampled at most once, evicted from the small profile (profile_self_class: cap 8, threshold 2), and never compiled for.

When that exit label was left unbound (bound only under #[cfg(feature = "profile")], so ordinary builds emitted a branch with a zeroed rel32 — a no-op), every miss fell through into the profiler instead, sampled the class twice back-to-back, crossed the threshold and compiled a specialization for every class that ever missed. ruby/spec’s concurrent-subclasses example compiled ~15,000 Object#should bodies (~300 MB) and timed the suite out. Fixed in #1158.

8. Measuring

Build with --features jit-log; jit_stats::dump() prints at exit:

version / salvage stats:
  class_version incs:                25022
  recovery attempts (class guard):   ...
    salvaged (re-resolution ok):     ...
  recovery attempts (loop guard):    ...
  recovery attempts (spec guard):    ...
  recovery attempts (const guard):   15740
    salvaged:                        10485
    value-compared sites:            13309
    fail: cache stale:               ...
    fail: value changed:             0
  whole recompiles  class-ver:       ...
  ...

Read it as: attempts are guard failures that reached a salvage entry, salvaged are the ones that kept their code, and the recompiles block is what was left over. fail: value changed staying at 0 over a whole spec run is the empirical case for the whole mechanism — the constant events were real, but never changed a folded value.

ruby/spec core (2,144 files / 23,034 examples), x86-64. Measured in two series, because the base moved in between — do not read across them:

Salvage, measured against the pre-#1156 base:

before salvageclass-version salvage (#1151, #1155)+ const-version salvage (#1157)
specialized recompiles (class ver)90,59368149
loop recompiles (class ver)12,39500
whole recompiles (const ver)4,1744,148155
JIT compile time22.4 s15.6 s12.8 s
peak code emission350.7 MB327.7 MB297.9 MB

Version-guard-driven recompiles across the whole run: 107,220 → 323.

The megamorphic gate (§7), measured against current master:

before #1158after #1158
Object#should whole compiles14,94530
JIT compile time23.1 s0.44 s
peak code emission318.4 MB10.6 MB

The gate dominates everything else: it was compiling one body per receiver class, which is why its emission dwarfs the recompile traffic salvage removes.

9. If you change this code

  • A new event that can change method resolution must bump the class version; one that can change constant resolution must bump the constant version and the right epoch (a name, or the wildcard when there is no single name).
  • A new compile path must register a salvage record, or its guard failures will recompile forever. The whole-method and loop paths do this in compile_patch / compile_partial_by_id.
  • A new question the compiler bakes in needs a new record and a new tier — do not extend an existing map with a differently-shaped invariant.
  • Never bind a guard’s miss-exit label inside a cfg block (§7). The snapshot side of a version compare is either the unit’s word or a registered patchable immediate (§2) — never an unregistered immediate, and never a compare emitted outside check_version on x86-64.

基本演算の再定義（BOP redefinition）

1 + 2 のような演算子式を、メソッド探索を挟まずインライン展開してよいのは 「Integer#+ が再定義されていない」という仮定が成り立つ間だけである。Ruby はその仮定をいつでも壊せる（class Integer; def +(o); …; end; end）ので、 処理系は「仮定を置く」「壊れたことを検知する」「壊れたあと辻褄を合わせる」の 3 点を用意しなければならない。

本書は monoruby の現行の仕組みをコードに即して記述し、CRuby の戦略と比べる。 粒度はどちらも (演算子, クラス) の組で、再定義の影響はその組を仮定した コードだけに及ぶ。

関連: doc/refinements.md §6.7（refinements と基本演算）、 doc/chain_deopt.md（実行中フレームの変換）、doc/jit_invariants.md、 doc/inline.md

1. 基本演算の表

globals/store/basic_op.rs の静的表 BASIC_OP_DEFS が、fast path が 仮定してよい (クラス, メソッド名) の組を列挙する。CRuby の vm_opt_method_defs と同型である。BasicOpTable はこれを intern したもので、 次を持つ。

フィールド意味
set / names表の組と、その名前だけの集合（「この定義は演算子に触れるか」の安い一次判定）
armedブートストラップ用ラッチ。ビルトイン自身の定義がこの表そのものなので、builtins/*.rb と gem のロードが終わるまで報告しない（Store::arm_basic_ops）
redefinedどれか 1 組でも置き換わったか。Rust 側の fast path はまずこれを読むので、何も再定義しないプログラムのコストはヘルパ呼び出しごとに bool 1 個
redefined_set置き換わった組（下の 2 つの和集合）。実行時ガードが知りたいのはこれ
globally_redefined_set / refined_set内訳。グローバルな再定義か、refinement だけによる無効化か（§5）
armed_funcsarm 時点での各組の解決先 FuncId（mixin 検知と JIT の解決に使う）
pending_warnings:performance 警告待ちの組
case_dispatch_offcase が値比較で分岐してよいクラスの === が置き換わったか（CRuby の opt_case_dispatch と同じく、立ったら戻らない）

判定キーが「上書きされたエントリ」ではなく「(クラス, メソッド) の組」で あることが要点である。Integer#! / #+@ / #~、NilClass#== などは そのクラスにエントリを持たない（Object / BasicObject からの継承）。 class Integer; def !; … は上書きではなく挿入なので、エントリに印を 付ける方式では原理的に検知できない。

2. 検知

メソッド表を変更する経路すべてに検知点がある。

  • insert_method / remove_method — def / define_method / alias / import_methods / undef_method（add_empty_method 経由）を 1 箇所で覆う。refinement のメソッドは refinement モジュール側の ClassId に入るので、refined_class() を引いて (refined_class, name) で照会する（§5）。
  • mixin — モジュールに後からメソッドが入った場合は insert_method → check_mixed_in_basic_op(module_id, name)、すでにメソッドを持つモジュール が後から差し込まれた場合は append_features / prepend_features → check_mixin_basic_ops(module)。

mixin で問うのは「モジュールがその名前を定義しているか」ではなく 「そのクラスは今もビルトインに解決するか」である。Comparable は < <= > >= == を定義し、Integer はブートストラップ以来それを include しているので、前者は include Comparable のたびに真になる。 mixin 検知は armed_funcs と現在の解決先を比べるので、Integer.prepend M （M が + を持つ）なら立ち、class Foo; include Comparable; end なら 立たない。回帰テストは basic_op.rs の a_mixin_that_displaces_nothing_keeps_the_basic_ops / a_prepend_that_displaces_the_builtin_retires_its_pair で、値ではなく表の 状態を直接確かめる（fast path が消えても答えは正しいので、値の比較では 検出できない）。

置き換わった組は Store::set_bop_redefine が記録し、pending_warnings に 積む。警告（Redefining 'Integer#+' disables interpreter and JIT optimizations）は Store の中では出せないので、Executor::invoke_method_added で出す。

3. VM 側の反応

VM の asm fast path はすべて fixnum 限定である。vm_binops_opt / vm_cmp_opt! / vm_neg … はどれも fixnum ガードで始まり、fixnum でない オペランドは Rust ヘルパ（add_values、cmp_lt_values、eq_values_vis、 not_value、get_index …）に落ちる。そこで反応は 2 段になっている。

  • asm 側（Integer のみ） — Codegen::bop_flags は JIT データ領域の 1 語で、 VmBop ごとに 1 ビットを持つ。asm の inline 計算を持つ 11 個 （+ - == != < <= > >= === +@ -@）の VM ハンドラは、自分の fixnum ガードの 直後で自分のビットを読み（x86-64 testq [rip+f], (1<<bit)、aarch64 ldr x9 / tbnz #bit）、立っていれば Rust ヘルパへ抜ける。CRuby インタプリタの BASIC_OP_UNREDEFINED_P と同じ配置である。~ と ! は inline 計算を持たず、残りの二項演算（* / % ** << >> & | ^）は最初から Rust ヘルパへ直行する。通常の実行ではこの検査のコストは測定にかからない。
  • Rust ヘルパ側（全クラス） — ネイティブに答えるアームに入る前に basic_op_redefined_for(受け手のクラス, 演算子名) を確かめ、置き換わって いれば本物のディスパッチに戻る（Executor::dispatch_redefined_op）。 ディスパッチ表を持たない Rust 側の fast path（runtime::{get_index, set_index} の Array#[] / Hash#[] / Array#[]=）も同じ表を読む。

ガードは「探索を飛ばした呼び出し元のための入口」*_values にだけ置き、 実装本体は無防備な *_values_raw に分けてある。ビルトインの Integer#+ の 本体（numeric.rs の binop! / unop!、integer.rs の cmpop! と % ** << >>、float.rs の比較と ==）は _raw を呼ぶ。ガードを実装側に 置くと、次のコードで __orig（= 元のビルトイン）に入った時点でガードが再び 発火し、名前 + で再ディスパッチして無限再帰になる。CRuby が BASIC_OP_UNREDEFINED_P を命令側（opt_plus）に置き rb_int_plus には 置かないのと同じ理由である。

class Integer; alias __orig :+; def +(o); __orig(o); end; end
1 + 2

回帰テストは aliasing_an_operator_before_redefining_it_does_not_recurse。 Array#sum や Numeric#angle のように探索せずに演算子を使う内部呼び出しは ガード付きの入口を使う（CRuby も同じ位置で BOP を見る）。

4. JIT 側の反応

JIT がガード無しで基本演算を仮定するのは、整数・浮動小数の算術／比較／ 定数畳み込みと単項演算だけである（state/binop.rs の binop_integer / binop_float / gen_cmp_* / unop_integer_* / unop_float）。メソッド 呼び出しに落ちるものはすべて class-version ガードで守られている （再定義は必ず class version を進める）。

  1. 仮定と記録 — inline 生成器の入口（fire_binary_inline / fire_unary_inline、融合 compare-and-branch も同じ）で JitContext::basic_op_assumable(class, op) を問い、生成器が成功した ときだけ record_bop_dep で (class, op) を記録する。解決には生の メソッド表ではなく arm 時のスナップショット（Store::basic_op_armed_func、 JitContext::resolve_basic_op）を使う（§6）。置き換わった組は仮定せず、 その演算だけ通常のメソッド呼び出しになるので、再定義後の再コンパイルは 健全で、他の演算子の inline は保たれる。
  2. 依存の保存 — 記録は jit_compile から ISeqInfo::bop_deps に 入る（self class をまたいで union）。
  3. 無効化 — set_bop_redefine は Store::evict_jit_code_for_bop(class, name) で、その組に依存した iseq（depends_on_bop）だけのコードを 捨てる（evict_jit_code）。捨てたメソッドは Codegen::rearm_jit_stub が wrapper のウォームアップ stub を戻してカウンタを COUNT_START_COMPILE に 再装填するので、次のウォームアップで再コンパイルされる。ループ本体は clear_loop_jit_entries がバイトコード内 LoopStart の [pc+8] を クリアする。このオペランドは三値（0 = 未コンパイル、1 = コンパイルが bail した恒久センチネル、それ以外が実エントリ）で、クリアするのは実エントリ だけである。恒久的に bail した本体は invalidate_jit_code で表し、 回復可能な evict_jit_code とは区別する。
  4. 実行中のフレーム — 捨てるだけでは、いまスタックで動いている JIT フレームが古いコードを実行し続ける。set_bop_redefine が bop_eviction_pending を立て、直後の Codegen::check_bop_redefine が それを消費して（エッジトリガ）、chain_deopt_into で全スレッドの スタック上の JIT フレームをインタプリタフレームへ変換する（各フレームの write-back を再生し、返りアドレススロットを共有 VM continuation stub に 書き換える。doc/chain_deopt.md §10）。他スレッドのフレームと、 セーフポイント poll で止まっているフレームの扱いは doc/chain_deopt.md §10.1。
  5. def 地点 — AsmInst::CheckBOP は JIT データ語のカウンタを コンパイル時の値と比べる（class-version ガードと同じ世代比較）。
  6. Ruby を走らせうるヘルパの直後 — 汎用演算子ヘルパ（多相な == など）、 文字列・正規表現の式展開（#to_s）、Hash リテラル（#hash）、Range リテラル（#<=>）、splat（#to_a）、多重代入（#to_ary）、when *ary、 再定義された Symbol#to_proc の &:sym は、フレームを積まないヘルパの中で Ruby を実行する。そこで再定義が起きても、ヘルパを呼んだフレームには 返りアドレスを保持する callee が無いので、4. の walk では変換されない。 これらの直後にも CheckBOP を置き（JitContext::check_bop_after_helper）、 出口は結果を書き戻して次の命令から VM で再開する。カウンタは無関係な 再定義でも進むので、出口は数回で再コンパイルする （RecompileReason::BopRedefined）。依存していない本体は新しいカウンタで 作り直され、以後は抜けない。splat と多重代入は Array をインラインで 扱う速い経路を持つので、比較はランタイム呼び出しの側にだけ置く （AsmInst::ToA / ExpandArray の bop）。回帰テストは tests/helper_bop_redefinition.rs。

fib(29)（release、x86-64）で測ると、fib が使わない演算子 （Float#+、Integer#~ / #| / #*、Array#[]）を再定義しても実行時間は 再定義なしと同じ（0.009 s）で、CRuby（0.051 s）でも同様に影響が無い。 fib 自身が使う演算子を再定義した場合は、その演算だけがメソッド呼び出しになる。

5. refinements

refinement による無効化は refined_set に入り、globally_redefined_set とは 分けて記録する。JIT は 2 段で問う（JitContext::assume_basic_op）。

  1. グローバルな再定義なら、どのスコープも逃れられないので inline しない。
  2. refinement 由来なら、コンパイル中のスコープの refinement set が実際に その組を解決し直すかだけを問う（basic_op_refined_in_scope）。refine していないスコープ（refine しないプログラムの全スコープを含む）は inline を維持する。

判定は「set のエントリのうち当該クラスを refine するものを辿り、その refinement モジュール（と ancestors）が当該名を持つか」で行い、クラス表しか 触らない（コンパイル中は CODEGEN を borrow_mut しているので、メソッド キャッシュを経由する解決は使えない）。判定は意図的に広めに倒してある。迷ったら 実呼び出しにするのは常に健全である。VM の asm ガードは呼び出し地点の文脈を 持たないグローバル語なので粗いままで、正しさはディスパッチが担保する。

呼び出しサイトの解決は「いま実行中のフレームが書いたスコープ」 （Executor::site_refinements）で行い、ネイティブフレームと Ruby 製コアの フレームは常に refinement なしになる（doc/refinements.md §6.10）。

6. Ruby で書いたビルトインと再定義

monoruby はコアの一部を Ruby で書いている（builtins/*.rb）。CRuby では C なので再定義の届かないコードが、ここでは届きうる。

class Integer; def <(o); :OV; end; end
[1, 2, 3].map { |x| x * 2 }
#   CRuby => [2, 4, 6]  (Array#map は C)

builtins/*.rb 由来のフレームには Meta::set_internal_builtin の 1 ビットが 立っており（$~ / $_ を持たせないためと、refinements を届かせないため）、 再定義もそこに届かせない。読む場所は 3 つである。

場所役割
Executor::dispatch_redefined_opVM ヘルパのガード。内部ビルトインのフレームからなら _raw へ落とす
JitContext::resolve_basic_opJIT の fast path 解決。生のメソッド表ではなく arm 時のスナップショット（Store::basic_op_armed_func）を引く
JitContext::basic_op_assumable上で解決したものをガード無しで inline してよい、という licence

CRuby 自身にも Ruby で書かれたコアメソッドがあり、Integer#times は <internal:numeric> のループで succ と < を呼ぶ。そのため CRuby では Integer#< を再定義すると 5.times が [] を返すが、monoruby の Integer#times はこの再定義の影響を受けない。CRuby のこの瑕疵は再現しない。

フレーム単位の束縛は「このファイルの演算子は全部ビルトイン束縛」としか 言えず、ライブラリ自身の帳簿（i += 1）と呼び出し側のための演算（sort の <=>）を区別できない。区別は手作業で保っている（EqSearch::new と op/sort.rs は意図的に束縛の外）。より細かい手段として、__add / __lt の ような再定義されない内部呼び出しを bytecodegen が通常の BinOp 命令に落とす 方式（intrinsic）がありうるが、builtins/*.rb の演算子約 1,000 箇所の多くは 呼び出し側の値を比較しており、intrinsic にしてはいけない。フレーム単位の 束縛を既定の安全側とし、実害が出た箇所から漸進的に intrinsic にする方針を とる（#1362 のレビューで決定）。

7. !=

CRuby にはどのクラスにも固有の != がなく、あるのは !(a == b) を計算する BasicObject#!=（rb_obj_not_equal）だけである。monoruby も同じで、 高速パスは次の形で持つ。

  • 表には (Integer|Float|String, "!=") を継承ペアとして置く （Integer#! と同じく、クラス自身にエントリは無い）。このペアが許可する のは「そのクラスに対する BasicObject#!= のインライン形」、つまり VM の fixnum 比較と JIT の object::object_ne である。
  • インライン形はビルトインの == を前提にするので、そのクラスの == の グローバルな再定義は != のペアも一緒に落とす（Store::set_bop_redefine）。 refinement による == の差し替えは連動させない。rb_obj_not_equal は == を rb_funcall で呼ぶので、refinement された == は見えないからである （実行時は Executor::eq_values_funcall、JIT は JitContext::funcall_eq）。
  • object_ne は受け手のクラスで分岐する。== が BasicObject#== / Symbol#== ならワード比較、Integer#== / Float#== なら数値比較、 String#== なら定数との比較（string_ne_gen）。クラスバージョンガード 付きの経路から入った場合は == の解決先を salvage 用に記録する （JitContext::assume_funcall_eq）。megamorphic なサイトの即値ビット比較 （opt_eq_assumable）は、!= のペアを持たない Symbol / NilClass / TrueClass / FalseClass について != が BasicObject#!= に解決する ことを確かめて記録する。
  • :performance 警告は != のペアには出さない（CRuby に != の basic op は 無く、opt_neq は BOP_EQ に乗る）。

インライン形を持たない ==（Struct / Array / Hash / Rational …）は BasicObject#!= の本体が呼ぶ。クラスごとのメモ（ClassInfo::eq_method_at、 Store::funcall_eq_entry）が == の解決先を持ち、それが引数 1 個の ネイティブメソッドなら、== を != 自身のフレームで実行する （Executor::default_ne_in_frame、Lfp::become_frame_of）。実行中フレームの Meta は == のものに替え、戻ったら != のものに戻すので、== の中から 出た例外のバックトレースは CRuby と同じ Struct#== → BasicObject#!= の 2 行になる。

8. hash / eql? は基本演算にしない

Hash / Set のルックアップは hash → eql? と連鎖するが、これらを表に 入れても速くならない。表は「この仮定を置いてよい」という許可と検知であって、 速度は仮定を使う fast path が出す。そして基本クラスのキーについては、 Value::hash_value / Value::eql（value.rs）が ObjTy で分岐して Rust 側で直接計算する fast path が既にあり、無条件に効いている。表に入れると set_bop_redefine が JIT まで巻き込むトリップワイヤが増えるだけである。

hash を定義していない素のオブジェクトについては、レシーバのクラスにおける hash の解決先がまだビルトインの Kernel#hash かを FuncId で比べ （Store::check_method、class-version キーのキャッシュ付き）、そうなら同じ digest を直接計算する。表は静的な (クラス, 名前) なので、ユーザ定義クラスが 自前の hash を持つ場合を表では捕まえられない。CRuby も rb_any_hash で 同じ特別扱いをしている。

9. CRuby の戦略との比較

  • ruby_vm_redefined_flag[BOP_xxx] — BOP ごとに 1 ワード、その中のビットが クラス（INTEGER_REDEFINED_OP_FLAG、FLOAT_… …）。vm_opt_method_defs （(クラス, メソッド名) → BOP）を rb_vm_check_redefinition_opt_method が メソッドの追加・削除のたびに引く。
  • インタプリタ — opt_plus 等の中で、オペランドの型チェックの後に BASIC_OP_UNREDEFINED_P(BOP_PLUS, INTEGER_REDEFINED_OP_FLAG) を毎回検査する。
  • YJIT / ZJIT — assume_bop_not_redefined() で「その (class, bop) は 未再定義」という invariant にコードブロックを登録し、再定義時はその invariant に依存するブロックだけを無効化する。
  • 通知 — -W:performance で警告を出す。
軸CRubymonoruby
表vm_opt_method_defsBASIC_OP_DEFS
VM の検査fast path 内のフラグ読み（BOP ごとの語 × クラスビット）asm は Integer の演算子ごとのビット、Rust ヘルパは組の集合
JITinvariant + 依存ブロックの無効化bop_deps + 依存 iseq の evict、実行中フレームは chain deopt
refinements—スコープ単位（§5）
通知-W:performance同じ警告

JIT に CRuby インタプリタ式の実行時チェックを入れる方式は採らない。いま 効いている定数畳み込みとレジスタ常駐が成立しなくなるためである。

10. 変更するときの確認

  1. コード生成の同一性 — BOP 再定義を含まないワークロードで --features emit-asm の出力が変更前とバイト単位で一致すること。
  2. 差分テスト — 演算子の再定義スイープ（再定義 × プローブ）と alias スイープの結果が CRuby と一致すること。
  3. 性能 — fib / optcarrot が baseline を維持し、無関係な演算子の 再定義で fib が遅くならないこと。

Chain deopt — converting suspended JIT frames to interpreter frames

Kind: reference. Chain deopt drops a whole suspended chain of compiled frames back to the interpreter in one step, without touching machine code. It is the only way an on-stack JIT frame is dropped to the interpreter. This document describes the mechanism, the frame-layout facts it depends on, and its three callers: basic-op redefinition, escalated side exits, and captures.

1. What this is for

A compiled frame that is suspended at a call cannot be protected by its callee’s guards. Three situations need such frames converted:

  • Basic-op redefinition. Redefining Integer#+ inside a callee makes the caller’s compiled continuation stale, because it inlined the builtin operator. Every suspended compiled frame on every thread must stop running its compiled body (doc/bop_redefinition.md, §10.1 below).
  • Side exits inside a compilation unit. Specialized callees, frameless bodies and yielded blocks are compiled into the caller’s unit, and the caller’s compiled continuation relies on facts derived from them: a narrowed return state (§6), and outer-frame Float locals that a specialized block reads and writes unboxed (§5 step 5, doc/trace_chain_joins.md §5). When such a callee deopts, the suspended frames above it in the same unit must not resume their compiled code.
  • Captures. A binding / eval that reaches a compiled frame through a path the JIT did not anticipate converts that frame first, so the capture reads homed slots (Codegen::convert_for_capture).

2. The mechanism

On a chain deopt every frame stays where it is on the stack. For each suspended compiled frame the walk:

  1. writes the frame’s register- and spill-resident state back into its local slots (boxing floats, materializing elided objects);
  2. rewrites the frame’s return-address slot to one shared continuation stub that resumes the interpreter after the call (§8.2).

Control then never re-enters the compiled body: as each callee returns, its ret lands in the stub. Because no machine code is rewritten, a compiled body that is still valid for future invocations survives.

3. Frame facts the mechanism relies on

3.1 The VM continuation after a call

The VM’s send handler resumes after a call by popping the cont frame (which holds the suspended pc), re-deriving the destination slot from the bytecode at that pc, storing the result and dispatching the next instruction. It is stack-driven and carries no per-site state. That sequence assumes a 2-unit send, though, while 1-unit operator sites (BinOp, Index, …) dispatch through the same JIT send emitter, which is why the walk targets a dedicated stub rather than the raw VM continuation (§8.2).

3.2 The suspended pc

AsmInst::ContFramePc { call_site_pc } stores the call-site pc into the outgoing cont-frame slot at every JIT call and yield emitter (ordinary send, send_specialized, generic and specialized yield). It is the slot Kernel#caller reads (Cfp::caller_pc_slot), and the stub reads it too.

3.3 What a write-back contains

WriteBack (jitgen.rs) has six kinds of entry:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fpr: Vec<(FPReg, Vec<SlotId>)>,                            // float -> one or more slots
literal: Vec<(Value, SlotId)>,
void: Vec<SlotId>,
gp: Vec<(GP, SlotId)>,
forward_kwrest: Vec<(SlotId, Box<[(IdentId, SlotId)]>)>,   // build the kwrest Hash
virtual_obj: Vec<(SlotId, VirtualSrc)>,                    // elided objects to allocate
}

Replaying one needs the WriteBack and the frame’s FP spill base, and virtual_obj / forward_kwrest need runtime calls (create_array or value_deep_copy, correct_rest_kw), so it is not a pure memory shuffle.

3.4 The registration key

A suspended frame is identified by the return address in its callee’s return-address slot, which is all the walk has to go on. Codegen::chain_deopt_table maps that return address to the site’s conversion stub and the calling frame’s depth in its compilation unit. AsmInst::ChainExit is pushed after the call, when the return address is no longer at hand, so it names its site through asm_return_addr_table, keyed by the site’s AsmEvict id.

4. Why the target is a stub, not the frame’s own deopt handler

Pointing the return-address slot at the call site’s own side-exit handler looks simpler, but it is wrong. The site’s write-back is captured after the result store (def_rax2acc_return) is modelled, so its handler assumes the callee’s return value is already in its slot. Entering it by ret skips that store and the return value is lost. The continuation stub performs the store itself (§8.2).

5. The steps

  1. Per-site conversion. Each call and yield site’s replay data is compiled into a conversion stub and registered in chain_deopt_table (§8.1).
  2. The continuation. One shared continuation stub per arch (§8.2).
  3. The walk. Codegen::chain_deopt_into walks the CFP chain from a given frame, converting each registered compiled frame (§8.5).
  4. Escalation. An interpreter-resuming side exit in a frame that is not its unit’s root runs the walk over its unit’s suspended frames before it resumes the interpreter (§8.5).
  5. Unboxed outer locals. A specialized block reads and writes an outer frame’s Float local directly in that frame’s FP save / spill area (LInst::LoadDynVarSpecF / StoreDynVarSpecF, a single f64 move at [rbp/x29 + offset + disp]). The claims are part of the abstract state (doc/trace_chain_joins.md §5). The frame’s slot does not hold the value meanwhile, so step 4 is what keeps a deopt below such a block sound: the walk boxes the value back into the slot before the interpreter can read it.

6. Return-state narrowing across a deopt-able callee

A specialized callee’s computed return state (for example Guarded::Class(Integer)) is consumed by the caller’s compiled continuation. A callee that deopts resumes in the interpreter and may return a value outside that class. The compiler used to widen the return state to Value for any callee that could deopt (frame_had_deopt, PR #505).

Escalation makes that widening unnecessary, and it is gone:

  • if the callee completes in compiled code, the inferred state was derived from exactly those paths, so it holds;
  • if the callee deopts, the escalated walk converts the caller as well, so the compiled continuation that consumed the narrowed state never runs.

Two conditions apply:

  • Every deopt below a consumer of a narrowed return state must escalate. This is enforced mechanically, not by review: the escalation count is stamped onto the AsmIr and every side-exit constructor reads it (§8.5).
  • has_exception_handler still widens. An exception raised and rescued inside the callee returns normally without a deopt, so the walk never fires and the happy-path inference would be wrong (issue #405). taint_for_unmodeled_rescue (state.rs) does this widening.

7. Why unboxed values stay out of the slots

Lfp::mark walks the frame’s register slots and marks each as a Value, so a raw f64 in a local slot would be scanned as a heap pointer. An unboxed outer local therefore lives in the owning frame’s FP save / spill area, and the specialized block is pointed there (§5 step 5). Anything that reads the slot expecting a boxed Value (a captured Proc, binding, generic block invocation, moving the frame to the heap, the interpreter after a deopt) must see the value boxed back first, which is what the walk and the capture conversion (§1) guarantee.

8. Implementation

8.1 The per-site conversion stub

At compile time each site’s ChainReplay (jitgen.rs: the site’s WriteBack, the frame’s spill base, the site’s UsingFpr, the call’s dst slot, and the call-site pc) is lowered by Codegen::gen_chain_replay_stub into a compiled conversion stub. The walk calls the stub with three frame pointers (callee bp, caller bp, caller Lfp), and the stub writes the suspended caller frame back.

The layout facts the replay depends on:

  • Every frame (VM, JIT, native wrapper) establishes bp == cfp + BP_CFP in its prologue (Cfp::frame_bp), so callee_rbp = callee_cfp + 8 and the caller’s saved bp is [callee_rbp].
  • Pool-resident floats live across the call in the cont-mode save area (fpr_save_with_cont / emit_fpr_save), allocated rsp-relative at the call: one 8-byte slot per set bit of the site’s UsingFpr, in bit order, at [rsp + 16 + 8i], which after the call and prologue is callee_rbp + 32 + 8i. The formula is the same on aarch64 (stp x29, x30 is the same 16-byte adjustment as call + pushq rbp), so one arch-neutral replay serves both.
  • Spilled FPRegs (ids >= PHYS_FPR_POOL) live base-relative in the caller frame, at [caller_rbp - (base - 24 + 8n)] (PhysMap::resolve).
  • The caller’s LFP is read through caller_cfp.lfp(), which follows a frame moved to the heap, as the emitted deopt write-back’s LFP register does.

virtual_obj / forward_kwrest call runtime::create_array (or value_deep_copy for a literal template) and runtime::correct_rest_kw, the same helpers and addressing that the deopt path’s gen_virtual_materialize / gen_forward_kwrest_materialize use. They run after the fpr / literal / void stores, so every deferred dst slot already holds nil and the frame stays GC-consistent across the allocating calls: slots always hold whole, valid (possibly stale) Values.

The stub reaches nothing on Codegen, so the walk applies each conversion in place, under the CODEGEN borrow it already holds. Frames are converted in walk order; the replays touch disjoint frames.

8.2 The shared continuation stub

The rewritten slots point at one stub per arch (gen_chain_cont_stub, emitted with the VM handlers, address in Codegen::chain_cont_stub). Its per-site input is a continuation word that the site’s conversion stub stores into the callee’s cont-frame pad slot (CFP+32, the second half of the 16-byte cont frame, which nothing reads on the normal return path). The word packs conv(dst) (0 = none) in the high 32 bits and the byte advance to the next instruction (pc.next() - pc: 16 or 32) in the low 32 bits, so 1-unit operator sites resume correctly.

Entered by ret, the stub:

  1. runs the pop_frame the hijacked ret skipped, derived from rbp/x29, restoring Executor::cfp and the LFP register;
  2. reads the call-site pc from the cont frame’s pc slot and the continuation word from the pad, then drops the cont frame;
  3. on the error signal (result 0), hands the call-site pc to entry_raise under each arch’s convention (x86-64 pc + 1 before the -16, aarch64 pc unchanged);
  4. otherwise stores the result into dst (if any) and resumes the fetch loop at pc + advance.

The stub never allocates. The pool registers are dead at the stub, because the replay consumed the save area.

8.3 Registration

Every call and yield site registers (AbstractState::chain_exit in jitgen/compile/method_call.rs, lowered to AsmInst::ChainExit / LInst::ChainExit, which emit no code). An unregistered site would be one that BOP eviction cannot convert, and §6’s return-state argument depends on registration too. tests/redefine.rs (redefine_bop_onstack_caller and others) checks the conversion positively: a suspended caller that resumed its compiled body would return the stale inlined result.

8.4 The unwind path goes through the rewritten slot

An exception does not bypass a rewritten slot. entry_raise with no in-frame handler unwinds by running the frame’s epilogue and reting with the error signal in rax/x0, so a propagating exception lands in the continuation stub, whose error branch re-raises from the converted frame at the call site (running its rescue / ensure there, or unwinding further). Non-local exits (MethodReturn, Break) take the same route, including method_return_specialized, whose ret lands in the stub through the slot of the outermost inlined call, the one whose dst the value is destined for.

8.5 The walk and escalation

Codegen::chain_deopt_into(cfp, frames) walks the CFP chain from cfp, rewriting each suspended caller through the return address its callee holds. frames bounds the walk (None walks the whole chain). Frames whose return address is VM code or an invoker are skipped, but the walk continues past them, since a chain may alternate VM and JIT frames. A frame converted by an earlier walk is skipped the same way, because its rewritten return address is the stub, a VM address. This matters: interpreted inner frames may have updated its slots through outer_lfp since, and a second replay would clobber them with stale floats.

Escalation is decided in one place. JitContext::chain_deopt_frames is the frame’s depth in its compilation unit; AsmIr::new stamps it onto the IR (AsmIr::chain_frames), and every side-exit constructor (new_deopt, new_deopt_with_pc, deopt_from_point, new_recompile_deopt, new_error) reads it, so no emitter can forget. A Deoptimize / RecompileDeoptimize / Error handler with a non-zero count calls runtime::chain_deopt(vm, frames) after its own write-back, before resuming the fetch loop or entering entry_raise. The walk starts at the deopting frame, so its own return-address slot is rewritten too, which converts its caller when the now-interpreted frame returns.

A frame at depth 0 is its unit’s root and does not escalate. Both things escalation protects are confined to one unit: a narrowed return state is applied only by def_rax2acc_return on the specialized path, and only a specialized block inside the unit reads an outer frame’s unboxed Float. An unrewritten slot of a root frame that raises lands in the caller’s compiled post-call error check, the ordinary JIT error path.

Error exits escalate because a raise can be rescued in-frame (an interpreter resume like any deopt) or unwind through the suspended callers (§8.4). Evict handlers are never entered: the AsmEvict id survives only as the key under which a call site’s return address is recorded (§3.4).

BOP eviction (Codegen::check_bop_redefine) walks whole chains, because it must convert frames across unit boundaries. A capture (Codegen::convert_for_capture) walks the capturing call site’s unit.

8.6 Where the code is

PieceLocation
ChainExitSpec (compile time), ChainReplay, gen_chain_replay_stub (x86-64)jitgen.rs (aarch64 form in arch/aarch64/compile/mod.rs)
AsmInst::ChainExit (registration, no code)jitgen/asmir.rs; lowered in jitgen/asmir/compile_shared.rs
LInst::ChainExitjitgen/lir.rs
Producers (call, specialized call, yield, specialized yield)AbstractState::chain_exit, jitgen/compile/method_call.rs
Shared continuation stubgen_chain_cont_stub (arch/x86_64/vmgen.rs, arch/aarch64/vmgen.rs), address in Codegen::chain_cont_stub
Deferred rest / kwrest materializationruntime::create_array, runtime::correct_rest_kw (codegen/runtime.rs)
Runtime table, the walkchain_deopt_table, register_chain_exit, chain_deopt_into, convert_for_capture (codegen.rs)
Escalation count and runtime entryJitContext::chain_deopt_frames (jitgen/context.rs), AsmIr::chain_frames (jitgen/asmir.rs), runtime::chain_deopt (codegen/runtime.rs)
Frame readers the walk usesCfp::return_addr, Cfp::frame_bp, Cfp::lfp (executor/frame.rs); the slot writes are emitted into the replay stub

9. Eager conversion

9.3 The whole chain is converted at deopt time

The walk replays every suspended frame’s write-back during the walk and points its return address at the shared continuation stub. A lazy form that wrote each frame back only when control returned to it is not sound: until then, anything reading an outer frame’s locals through outer_lfp (a block body, binding, a backtrace) would read stale slots, which matters as soon as a frame’s slots do not hold its locals (§5 step 5). The eager form also needs no per-site handlers: the rewritten slot always points at the one shared stub, and the per-site part is the conversion stub the walk calls.

10. Chain conversion replaced code patching

Before chain conversion existed, a basic-op redefinition dropped suspended frames by patching each call’s return continuation in the code with a jump to that site’s Evict handler. Chain conversion replaced that entirely:

  • a compiled body still valid for future invocations survives, because no machine code is rewritten;
  • aarch64 loses a self-modifying-code path and its writable / I-cache dance around every patched word;
  • there is one walk to reason about instead of two that must agree.

10.1 The other threads’ chains, and the frame at a poll

A basic-op redefinition is the one caller of the walk whose stale frames are not all on the redefining thread’s stack. Every other Ruby thread is suspended under it (a kernel thread waiting for the GVL, doc/threads.md §12), and each may hold compiled frames that inlined the operator just replaced. check_bop_redefine therefore walks every chain: its own, then the chain of each executor scheduler::suspended_executors returns (the context a thread parked or yielded in, published by park, pass and without_gvl, followed by its parent_fiber links, so a thread parked inside a fiber contributes the fiber’s frames and the resumer’s). Those frames are as quiescent as the caller’s own.

The walk converts callers, through the return address their callee holds, so a chain’s innermost compiled frame is beyond it. On the redefining thread that frame is the one running the def, and AsmInst::CheckBOP after MethodDef handles it. On another thread the innermost frame is whatever it let go from: a call site (sleep, Queue#pop, Thread.pass, all of which push a frame whose return address the walk finds) or a safepoint poll (a timeslice tick or a signal taken at a LoopStart / method-entry poll), where there is no callee frame. That frame leaves from the poll itself: ISeqInfo::bop_evictions counts evictions per iseq, executor::execute_gc snapshots the polling frame’s count on entry and, if it moved while the frame was away, returns POLL_DEOPT instead of nil; the compiled poll’s cold path compares for it and jumps to the poll’s own deopt exit (AsmInst::ExecGc::deopt, AsmIr::new_poll_deopt), resuming the interpreter at LoopStart or at the instruction after InitMethod. That exit does not set had_deopt: by the time it can fire, the walk has already rewritten every caller of the frame, and marking it would put had_deopt on every body, since every method entry polls. The same exit covers the redefining thread’s own poll when a trap handler or a finalizer run from the poll does the redefinition.

A fiber that is suspended (not parked) inside one of those threads stays out of reach: it is in no chain the walk sees, and it polls nothing until resumed. Regression tests: builtins::thread::tests::bop_redefinition_reaches_* (parked, parked in a fiber, yielded through Thread.pass, preempted at a poll).

Reading the deopt log (--features deopt)

What a record looks like

<-- deopt occurs in <Array#each> FuncId(2251).
      [:00019] %1 = %1 + %2   [Integer][Integer]   exit: deopt (chained)
      guard: monoruby/src/codegen/jitgen/asmir/compile_shared.rs:541:34
      exit emitted by: monoruby/src/codegen/jitgen/compile/method_call.rs:973:24
      cause: class version
fieldmeans
first linethe frame that deoptimized
[:NNNNN]its bytecode index, and the TraceIR at that index
exit:what the handler is — deopt, evict, or recompile[reason], plus (chained)
guard:the lowering site of the guard that actually branched
exit emitted by:the front-end site that decided a deopt was needed here
cause:the operand the guard was looking at, or a name when there is none

guard: is the field to read first. It identifies the branch, not the handler — see below for why those differ.

Why it is built the way it is

The cause column used to be “whatever sat in rdi when the side exit ran”. That was wrong in two independent ways, and the two together produced four consecutive misdiagnoses during the activerecord deopt investigation:

The value was stale. The handler read rdi after the deopt write-back, which calls into C (f64_to_val, create_array, …) and clobbers the register file. Most records printed UNDEFINED — how a zero word renders — so the column was noise dressed as data.

The guard was unidentifiable. Deopt exits are deduplicated by (pc, write_back, chain), and a single AsmDeopt is handed to several guards even before that. Neither the handler nor the AsmDeopt index names the branch that was taken. Two guards at one pc are one handler, and the log could not tell them apart.

So identity is recorded where the branch is. Every lowering site that asks for a deopt label gets a trampoline of its own:

site_NNN:
    movq [rbx + EXECUTOR_DEOPT_CAUSE], <cause register>
    movl [rbx + EXECUTOR_DEOPT_SITE],  <site id>
    jmp  <deduplicated handler>

rbx is &mut Executor for the whole body, so this costs no scratch register, no stack traffic, and — at a point where a guard has just done its compare — no flag-clobbering instruction. Recording the operand before the write-back is what makes the value trustworthy, which in turn lets the log call stay where it always was: after the write-back, with nothing live in registers.

Handlers stay deduplicated. Only the trampolines multiply, at ~20 cold-page bytes each.

The invariant

The only way to reach a deopt handler from a JIT body is Codegen::deopt_label, and it demands a DeoptCause.

SideExitLabels has no Index<AsmDeopt> impl, and deopt_label has no default for cause. A new guard that skips the question does not compile.

Choosing a cause: for the label this call returns, is a meaningful operand present on every path that jumps to it? If some edge leaves the register undefined, the honest answer is DeoptCause::Static("…").

variantwhen
Value(r)a Ruby Value is in r on every edge
ValueVsBaked(r, v)…and the guard compared it against v, baked at compile time
Raw(r)non-Value bits (pointers, byte counts); printed as hex, never decoded
Static(s)no operand: global state (version word, BOP flag, counter), an unconditional deopt, or an unboxed float

Floats are deliberately Static. An FPReg is virtual — resolving one needs the frame’s base_stack_offset, since a spilled float lives on the stack rather than in an xmm — and threading a frame through every guard’s lowering to recover an operand for two call sites is not worth it.

What the log will not do

It will not decode a word it cannot vouch for. A Value cause is checked (Value::debug_check) before it is decoded, and the raw bits are always printed alongside. The write-back between capture and log can run a GC, so an object reachable only from the guard’s register may be gone by then; such a word reads as <not a Value> rather than as a plausible lie.

It will not attribute a branch it did not see. A handler entered without a trampoline — an evict resuming through a patched return address, say — reports guard: unknown (handler entered without a trampoline). The site id is taken and cleared on every read, so a later entry cannot inherit an earlier one’s identity.

It will flag its own contradictions. A ValueVsBaked guard that reports a miss on bits equal to what it compares against prints !!! guard reported a miss on equal bits. That exact contradiction — a guard appearing to fail against the value it was testing for — is what cost four hypotheses before the log could state it.

Scope

Everything here is cfg(feature = "deopt"). Normal builds emit byte-identical code: deopt_label compiles to the bare handler label and the cause argument is discarded. profile-only builds keep their original call site.

aarch64 records every deopt but not the branch that took it. a64_gen_deopt calls log_deoptimize at the x86 position (after the write-back, before the chain walk), so deopt builds print each record with its bytecode index and exit kind, and profile builds fill the deoptimization table. There are no trampolines, so every aarch64 record reads guard: unknown (handler entered without a trampoline). Until the call existed, an aarch64 guard that failed on every execution was invisible to both builds.

The trampoline cannot be copied from x86 as is. x86 parks it on the cold page; aarch64 guards reach their handlers with tbz/tbnz (±32 KiB), which is why the handlers are emitted as islands within reach (a64_thunk_side_exits), and a cold-page trampoline would be out of range. A port has to place the trampolines in the same islands as the handlers.

レシーバ多相なコールサイト

Kind: reference。レシーバのクラスが実行ごとに変わるコールサイトを JIT が どう扱うかをまとめる。観測（VM の多相検出と PMC）、消費（集合ガード、PIC、 二項演算・[] の dispatch、generic send の残余）、残っている設計上の論点の 順に述べる。

自フレームの self クラスによる本体の切り替え（メソッド入口のクラス dispatch stub と megamorphic gate）は別の仕組みで、docs/src/jit-compiler.md と codegen/class_dispatch.rs を参照。

1. 背景: 単相前提のガード

JIT のメソッド呼び出しは、VM のインラインキャッシュ（receiver class → FuncId、1 エントリ）を元に組み立てる。キャッシュされたクラスでレシーバ クラスガードを発行し、ガードの内側で FuncId を確定させ、インライン生成器 （inline_info.get_inline）か直接呼び出しへ落とす。単相のサイトではこれで 十分だが、多相のサイトではガード失敗のたびに side exit する。

典型は nil との二相である。Ruby の慣用句はレシーバが nil かもしれない 場所でこそメソッドを呼ぶ。

return 1 if left.nil?        # left は Array か nil（binarytrees の item_check）
limit = to unless to.nil?    # to は Numeric か nil（numeric.rb の step）
if by == nil ...

二項演算子でも同じことが起きる。rubykon の group_id_of(id) == captured.identifier は左辺が Array の要素で、ヒットなら Integer、 ミスなら NilClass になる。

2. VM による多相の検出

VM は実行時に多相を検出し、バイトコードの opcode_sub バイトに書き込む。 TraceIR はそれを polymorphic として読む。

経路クラスの保存opcode_sub の検出
メソッド呼び出し slow path（vmgen/method_call.rs）✓✓
binop / cmp generic（vm_generic_binop → vm_save_binary_class）✓✓
binop / cmp fixnum fast path（vm_save_binary_integer）上書きのみ✗（多相サイトは必ず generic を通るので無害）
unop generic（vm_save_lhs_class / a64_save_lhs_class）✓✓
Index / StoreIndex（VM 命令内で vm_save_binary_class を流用）✓✓

callsite はメソッド呼び出しのほか UnOp / BinOp / Cmp / Index / StoreIndex にもあり（bytecodegen/encode.rs の new_callsite + new_callsite_map_entry）、IseqInfo::callsite_map で CallSiteInfo に 届く。例外は RescueTEq だけである（rescue 節のマッチ専用で IC を持たない）。

3. 集合ガード — 観測クラスが同じメソッドに解決するサイト

観測したクラスがすべて同じ native メソッドに解決するサイト（nil?、 is_a?、frozen? …）は、クラス集合のメンバーシップガード GuardClassIn （pmc_same_target_classes）の後で通常呼び出しを出す。FuncId は jit_check_call で再計算し、PMC が保存した値は使わない。ガードを通った クラスはすべて同じメソッドに解決し直してあるので、クラスごとに呼び分ける 必要がない。iseq ターゲットはレシーバクラスで特殊化されるため対象外である。

集合ガードの後でもインライン生成器は発火しうる（§9）。

4. PIC — クラスごとに解決先が違うサイト

観測クラスが別々のメソッドに解決するサイトは、compile/pic.rs が N-way の クラス dispatch を出す（compile_pic_call、最大 PIC_WAYS = PMC_WAYS アーム）。

        load recv -> rdi
        guard_class_version                 (全アームを支配する 1 回)
        br_class_ne rdi, C0 -> L1
        <call C0#name>
        br merge
  L1:   br_class_ne rdi, C1 -> L2
        <call C1#name>
        br merge
  L2:   guard_class rdi, C2 -> 残余         (最終アーム)
        <call C2#name>
  merge:

合流は compile/dispatch.rs のブロック内マージで、宣言型である。分岐の 前にオペランドをスタックへ flush し、dst を未知の Value とし、アームが 任意の Ruby を実行しうるのでキャッシュ済みの invariant をすべて落とした 状態を合流状態として先に決める。各アームはそこへ bridge する （AbstractState::gen_bridge_all）。アームの事後状態が揃っている必要は ないので、ゲートは健全でない形とコンパイルを abort させる形だけを除外すれば よい。

PMC が 1 クラスしか持たないサイトは、abstract state がレシーバを特定でき なくても単相とみなして単一ガードのままにする。実測ではこれがゲートの拒否 理由の大半を占める。

5. 設計上の論点

5.1 合流状態の精度

宣言型の合流は精度を失う。2 つのアームがどちらもレジスタに Fixnum を 残しても合流でボックス化される。結果が不透明な Value で終わる呼び出しの dispatch では損失はないが、数値の dispatch（fixnum アーム / float アーム / generic 残余）では効く。格子には LinkMode::Sf(fpr, SfGuarded::FixnumOrFloat) （ボックス化したスロット + 生きた float の影）という要素があるので、 declare_merge に呼び出し側が合流形を渡せるようにするのが次の段階である。

5.3 abstract state に union を持たせるか

Guarded 格子は単一クラス（+ Fixnum/Float 系の特例）しか表現しない。 recv_class ∪ NilClass のような 2 要素 union を表現できれば、非 nil 側の 下流（unless to.nil? の then 側など）を分岐条件から recv_class 単相へ 絞り直せる。truthiness 分岐で nil を落とす flow-sensitive な絞り込みは、 集合ガードとも PIC とも直交する改善である。ただし格子の拡張は merge / bridge 全体に波及するので、工数は最も大きい。未実装。

5.5 採らない案

  • nil? のガード全廃（値比較のみ） — 「どのクラスも nil? を再定義して いない」というグローバル性質が必要で、Kernel を include しない BasicObject 系レシーバ（nil? は NoMethodError になるべき）で誤答する。 クラスガードは第三のクラスに対する安全網として残す。

6. 二項演算子と [] の dispatch

二項演算子の多相サイトは、ホットなクラスをインラインのアームに、それ以外を generic な C 呼び出しの残余に振り分ける（binary_dispatch、 dispatch_inline_class）。片方だけでは足りない。単一クラスガードで インライン化すると他のクラスで毎回 side exit し（rubykon の == 1 箇所で 180 万回）、generic な比較だけにするとホットなクラスまで C 呼び出しになる。

  • アームのクラスはインラインキャッシュではなく PMC から選ぶ。キャッシュは 最後に来たクラスを持つだけで、交互に来るサイトでは偶然に左右される。
  • nil が観測されたサイトは、nil に生ビット比較のアームを与える。nil の シェアが小さくても、単相ガードのままなら現れるたびに side exit するため、 2 番手のシェアによらず dispatch する。nil 以外の少数派は 1/8 のシェア規則に 従う（そのアームは generic な呼び出しなので、相応の頻度が要る）。
  • Integer のアームガードは fixnum タグを見るので、Bignum は deopt せず 残余アームに落ちる。IntegerOverflow の exit が印を付けたサイト （compile_binary 2a）は、PMC によらず Integer のアームを持つ。

単相の BinCmp サイトは、ガード失敗が温まると RecompileReason::BecamePolymorphic で再コンパイルし、上の dispatch に移る （RecvMissMode::PartB）。

多相な [] サイトは、インライン化するクラスのアームと invoke_method(:[]) の残余からなる 2 アームの dispatch になる （compile/index.rs）。

7. PMC の記録と profile ダンプ

  • 格納: CallSiteInfo::pmc: PolyCache（globals/store.rs）。最大 PMC_WAYS = 4 エントリの PolyCacheEntry { recv, arg, fid, count } と、 5 個目以降の観測を数える overflow カウンタ（megamorphic）。キーは MethodCall / UnOp = レシーバのみ、BinOp / Cmp / Index / StoreIndex = レシーバ + 第一引数。
  • 記録点（すべて slow path、定常状態のコストはゼロ）:
    • MethodCall: runtime::find_method（単一エントリキャッシュのミス時）で class_for_ic と解決済み FuncId を記録する。cacheable = false （frame-dependent な super）は記録しない。
    • BinOp / Cmp / Index / StoreIndex: vm_save_binary_class / a64_save_binary_class の「初回 population」と「多相への遷移」の 2 分岐 から runtime::pmc_record_binary(vm, globals, pc, old_lhs, old_rhs) を 呼ぶ。置き換えられた旧ペアも一緒に記録する。fixnum fast path は IC に 記録せずスタンプするので、置き換えの瞬間がそのペアを PMC に残す唯一の 機会である。一度も置き換えられなかったスタンプは PMC に載らないが IC には 残るので、消費側は IC の現内容と PMC の和集合を観測集合として扱う。
    • UnOp: vm_save_lhs_class / a64_save_lhs_class から pmc_record_unary。
  • count は slow path での観測数であって呼び出し総数ではない。
  • ダンプ: --features profile の終了時統計（Store::show_stats）の 「polymorphic method cache」節。サイト数（recorded / polymorphic / megamorphic）と、観測数順の多相サイト上位 40 件を class(/arg)(=resolved-func) xN の形で表示する。

PMC のエントリは class-version ガードの傘の下にある（再定義でサイトを 含む本体が無効化される）ので、エントリ個別の無効化は要らない。

9. 集合ガードの背後のインライン生成器

InlineGen（globals.rs）は受け手と引数のクラスを Option<CachedClass> で受け取る。生成器を発火させること自体が「実行時に受け手がどのクラスでも、 このサイトの名前はこの生成器のメソッドに解決する」という呼び出し側の保証で あり、集合ガードと PIC のアームはこれを満たす。Some(class) はクラスが 静的にも確定していることを加え、None は確定していないことを示す。生成する コードがクラスに依存する生成器は None で辞退し（false を返す）、値の 表現だけを読む生成器（nil?、frozen?（emit_frozen_pred）、__id__、 object_id）は発火し続ける。登録経路は 1 つで、クラス非依存版を別に 登録する必要はない。

is_a? / instance_of? / respond_to? 系は静的なクラスで畳み込むので、 多相サイトでは辞退してビルトイン呼び出しになる。

10. generic send の残余

PIC の最終アームで学習の余地がない（PMC 満杯・overflow）とき、および PMC が 既に多相を観測しているサイトの単相 / 集合ガードのミスは、deopt ではなく generic send の残余に落ちる。多相サイトが永久に deopt し続けることはない。

  • 形: 残余は dispatch.rs の宣言型マージの 1 アーム （RecvMissMode::Residual、pic.rs の最終アーム / method_call_with_residual）。ガードのミス先が残余ラベルになる。
  • 探索: GuardSendResolvable がレシーバクラスを 1-way キャッシュ （runtime::GenericSendCache: class, class version, fid）と照合し、ミスなら jit_generic_send_check で探索して書き戻す。解決できない（未定義・private・ method_missing 経由）か、呼び先が binding / eval 系の効果を持つときは 0 を返し、そのときだけ deopt する。
  • 呼び出し: GenericSend はキャッシュの fid から FuncData を取り、 wrapper 経由で呼ぶ（self 特化本体へは wrapper が dispatch する）。splat・kw・ ブロックのない 8 引数以下の呼び出しは、呼び先が単純なシグネチャ （META_KIND の simple bit と FUNCDATA_MIN == pos_num）ならインラインで コピーし、それ以外は vm_handle_arguments で束縛する。
  • 間接的な binding: 呼び先が send や Method#call のように名前で 呼び戻す builtin だと、admission の判定をすり抜けて Kernel#binding に 届き、JIT フレームがヒープへ昇格する。残余アームでは no_capture_guard を 落とし、send 後の capture ガードで deopt してヒープ側のローカルを読む。
  • ... 転送サイト: 実行時の束縛は VM と同じ vm_handle_arguments なので、 転送された rest が実 Array でも遅延転送マーカーでもそのまま束縛できる。 JIT 側では settle_operands_for_runtime_binder が elided のままの rest / **kwrest を実体化し、K1 の kw スキップに拒否権を出す （arg_forwarding_jit.md）。
  • メソッド本体に直接書かれた super も対象になる （generic_send_eligible）。ブロック付きの呼び出しは対象外である。

ミスの扱いは RecvMissMode が決める。PMC がまだ単相のサイトのミスは 再コンパイルを伴う exit（Learn）で、多相への切り替えの機会を与える。多相の ゲートが既に辞退したサイトでは、再コンパイルしても同じ本体になるので通常の deopt にとどめる。

テスト: pic.rs の pic_*、pic_overflow_generic_residual（アリティ差・kw・ splat+ブロック引数・method_missing・private・alias tag binding）、 pic_residual_indirect_binding、mono_guard_generic_residual。

Escape analysis: eliding Array and Range literals and *rest

[a, b].max, [:get, :head].include?(verb), [x, y].first, (lo..hi).include?(v), case v when 1..5: an Array or Range literal that is built only to be the receiver of one call, and is dead right after it. The JIT does not allocate such a literal when it is compiled. It records it in the abstract state as an elided object and decides at its use whether the object is needed at all. The same object can be handed, still elided, into a specialized callee’s parameter — as the literal argument of size([a, b]), or as the *rest parameter the callee binds f(a, b) into (§6).

The pattern-specific part is data: what a callee may be handed instead of a real Array is its receiver escape summary, declared next to the builtin.

Source: codegen/jitgen/compile/escape.rs; the state half in state/slot.rs (SlotState::virtuals, LinkMode::from_caller) and state.rs; the side-exit half in WriteBack::virtual_obj (codegen/jitgen.rs, and a64_gen_virtual_materialize on aarch64); the summaries in builtins/array.rs and builtins/range.rs (init_recv_escape, init_recv_escape_ruby) and executor/inline.rs (RecvEscape, ElementsOp); the Range runtime helpers in codegen/runtime.rs (create_range, range_cover, range_fold).

The scope is deliberately narrow. Until 2026-11 the analysis also kept objects in local variables (with a per-local scratch window reserved by the bytecode compiler), carried them through forward merges and loop heads, handed a returned object back to the caller’s slots, folded x[i] on an elided Array, folded lookups on Hash literals and elided **kwrest parameters. Measured with each stage switched off, none of them moved any of the 22 ruby-bench benchmarks (cachegrind instruction counts), while together they were about 1,700 lines across the bytecode compiler, the merge / loop machinery and both backends, so they were removed. What is left is the part that pays: a literal consumed where it is built, *rest and ... handed into callees, and Range literals.

1. The elided object

Three instructions and a method entry can produce one:

WhereVirtualSrcCondition
%d = array[%s..%s+n]Slots { src, len, callid }no splat; %d and the elements are temporaries, the elements dead once the literal is built (at or above the stack top)
%d = literal[...]Literal(template)%d is a temporary; the template is a plain Array whose elements are all immediates, or a Range whose endpoints are immediates
%d = %s..%e / %s...%eRange { start, end, exclude_end }%d is a temporary; each endpoint is a compile-time Fixnum or nil (RangeEnd::Const) or a slot proven to hold a Fixnum (RangeEnd::Slot), so building the Range later can neither dispatch <=> nor fail (§7)
a specialized callee’s parameterCallerSlots { src, len, base }, or the caller’s Literalthe caller handed the object over (§6)

The slot %d becomes LinkMode::V and the object lives only in SlotState::virtuals. A Slots object’s element slots, and a Range object’s endpoint temporaries, are pinned (VirtualSrc::own_slots): clear_above_next_sp leaves them alone although the bytecode considers them dead, because they are the object’s contents. A Literal object needs no storage: its contents are the template’s.

The object ends in one of four ways.

  • Consumed by its use (§2): the Array is never allocated.
  • Handed over to a specialized callee as a parameter (§6), where it ends in one of these ways again.
  • Dropped: its slot is overwritten, or falls above the stack top, without being read; or it is a parameter nothing reads any more; or it is the discarded result of a specialized callee (§8). Nothing ever saw it.
  • Materialized: allocated after all, by exactly the code the literal would have run (NewArray / DeepCopyLit, CreateArrayFrom over the caller’s window, or CreateRange from the endpoints), at the point where something could first observe it.

2. Consuming uses

A use that may consume the object is a method call with it as the receiver, and nowhere else in the call’s operands (may_consume_virtual); for a Literal also the %d = %base[%idx] index instruction (consume_virtual_index), which is Array#[] resolved the same way; for a Range also the === comparison with it on the left (consume_virtual_teq: the case … when lo..hi opcode and the explicit (lo..hi) === v), which is Range#=== resolved the same way. The call resolves the method on the object’s class (VirtualSrc::class_id) under the class-version guard and reads the callee’s RecvEscape:

  • elements: Some(op) — an allocation-free lowering over the object’s elements, for a Slots or CallerSlots object and an argument-less, block-less call. Min / Max compare the elements in their slots (ArrayMinMax, over the frame’s own slots or the caller’s window), in the order the call it stands for would: best <=> v for Array#min, v <=> best when the call is written on the literal itself ([a, b].max, CRuby’s opt_newarray_send; CallSiteInfo::newarray_recv, MinMaxOp) — which is the operand a failed comparison names (#2007); Size, Empty are answered at compile time; First, Last are a copy of one element slot (LoadCallerSlot for a handed-over object). Over the endpoints of an elided Range (Const or Slot), RangeCover (include?, member?, cover?, ===) is two tagged compares inline for a Fixnum argument — the tag bit is the same on both sides, so Fixnums order as tagged words, and a nil endpoint bounds nothing — with runtime::range_cover behind it for any other argument; RangeSize, RangeCount, RangeSum, Min, Max, First, Last are folded at compile time for constant endpoints (runtime::range_fold) and go through a helper otherwise; RangeBegin, RangeEndpoint, RangeExcludeEnd are the endpoint itself (plan_range_op, emit_range_plan). Where the in-place answer does not apply — a non-numeric argument, a nil endpoint the method rejects, a redefined Integer#<=> — the helper builds the Range and dispatches the resolved method on it, exactly the call that would have been made. A parameter stays elided after such a use if it is still live (the next args.size is free too); a temporary is done. None of these applies when a positional argument of the call is itself an elided object ((1..10).cover?(1..5), Range#cover? being a Ruby method that takes it, §6): each object is judged on its own (may_consume_virtual), but the lowering here reads the argument slots as values, and an elided argument’s slot holds none. The call is then the one that takes both — the receiver is materialized (a frozen literal is its template, at no cost) and the argument handed over (consume_virtual’s args_elided).
  • transparent: true — the callee never mutates, stores or returns its receiver, nor returns an Enumerator over it, in any argument form. A Literal object’s copy is then indistinguishable from the template to the callee, so the call is compiled as usual with the receiver slot bound to the template (LinkMode::C). Arguments and a block literal are fine: only the receiver’s identity is at stake. The receiver slot must be dead after the call, so the template never becomes visible to later code. Array#[] is one of these, so [:a, :b, :c][i] indexes the template.

Anything else materializes the object and compiles the call as before.

A yield [e1, .., en] (n >= 2, no splat) is a consumer too (yield_expanded_for). Bytecodegen gives such a site an expanded twin, CallSiteInfo::yield_expanded: the call site of yield e1, .., en, whose arguments are the temporaries the Array literal is built from (the yield’s argument slot + 1 ..), with the same result slot. When the block is the literal one specialized in place and auto-splats a lone Array argument (FuncInfo::single_arg_expand: block style, more than one positional parameter) and takes no keywords, it binds the elements exactly as it would bind the Array, so the JIT yields through the twin and the Array is never built (Hash#each’s yield [key, value] into { |k, v| }). The object stays registered until the block’s arguments are filled: a frameless block’s redo exit hands the original yield back to the interpreter, which reads the Array from its slot, so that exit materializes it.

So is a multiple assignment from the object (consume_virtual_expand): a, b = [x, y] expands it straight into its targets — a template’s constants, copies of the element slots, nil past the end — with the object gone afterwards. The targets are the temporaries right above the object, overlapping the element slots, so the copies run far end first (a memmove) when the targets lie above the elements.

A Mov from a parameter’s object into a temporary (args.include?(a + 1) evaluates its receiver into a temporary before the argument) moves the object when the parameter is dead afterwards, and otherwise gives the temporary a second view of it when the first reader of the temporary is a call that only reads its receiver’s elements (alias_consumed_by_call; consume_virtual_mov). The two views are never told apart: such a method neither mutates nor lets out its receiver.

The class-version guard is emitted while the object is still registered, so a redefinition (class Array; def max = self; end) deopts with the object materialized and the interpreter calls the new method on a fresh Array.

Adding a consumer is a summary entry. An entry is a promise about every argument form of the method; take qualifies (take(n) larger than the size returns a dup), each does not (it returns self), index does not (blockless, argument-less it returns an Enumerator over self). The Range table (builtins/range.rs, init_recv_escape_ruby) is registered on the resolved methods after builtins/range.rb is loaded (from Executor::new), since that file defines most of them (===, include?, cover?, size, sum, min, max, …) over the builtins; a Range is immutable, so every method of its own that returns neither self nor an object holding it (each, step, % do) is transparent.

3. When an object is materialized

settle_virtuals runs before every instruction. An object not consumed by the instruction is

  • dropped if the instruction does not read it and it is dead after it;
  • otherwise materialized if any of these hold:
    • the instruction reads it (a Mov, an argument, a ret, an index base);
    • the instruction could overwrite an element slot (its stack top reaches the elements: bytecode temporaries are only written by pushes), or writes a local that is an elided Range’s endpoint;
    • the instruction ends the basic block;
    • the object is in a temporary and the instruction can run Ruby code or reach a call — only Mov, Literal, FrozenLiteral, Array, the InlineCache word and instructions writing nothing but a plain destination are survivable (virtual_survives, defined_slot).

settle_virtuals_at_bb_end does the same after an instruction that ends its block by falling through.

No object crosses a block boundary. Every block ends with its live objects materialized and its dead ones dropped, so a branch entry never carries one and joins, loop heads and branch bridges reconcile nothing. The one entry that does bring objects is a method’s start, into its first block, with the parameters its caller handed over (§6); settle_entries keeps those, and a method whose first block is a loop head is handed nothing (caller_slots_ok). At any other merge settle_entries materializes whatever an entry still holds, on that entry’s bridge, as a safety net; it finds nothing there in practice.

An intra-block dispatch (a class dispatch, a polymorphic call, a generic binary operator: declare_merge) is a merge of its own, and its arms may emit the CondBr that follows it (CondBrSink), which makes the instruction the block’s last. So declare_merge materializes an elided object among the operands (no arm takes one over), and, under a sink, settles every live object of the frame as the block’s end would (settle_virtuals_before_branch).

A producer lowered with a CondBr as its sink without a dispatch — a fused comparison, a predicate call — may leave its answer in the condition flags, and nothing may be emitted between it and the branch. The block-end materialization the CondBr would perform is an allocation call that clobbers them (issue #1837: [[1], c ? [7] : [6]] branched on whatever the allocator left), so it is done before the producer instead (settle_virtuals_for_sink): every object the producer does not read is dropped if dead after the branch and materialized otherwise. materialize_virtual asserts (debug) that no condition is pending.

A parameter holding a handed-over object (§6) follows the same rules but one: it survives its frame’s calls. Its elements are in the caller’s frame (or are a template), which no callee can reach, and the callee gate guarantees that nothing in the body can observe the parameter slot behind the compiler’s back. It is dropped once nothing can read it any more (local_live_after, §10).

The consequences are what keep the mechanism small:

  • A merge never joins an elided object.
  • A suspended frame owes only objects whose elements are safe. A temporary’s object never lives across a call; a handed-over object’s elements are in the caller’s frame, so the chain-deopt replay stub (gen_chain_replay_stub) materializes CallerSlots (through the frame’s saved bp or its window offset) and Literal entries.
  • Liveness comes from the stack top. The bytecode’s own per-instruction stack top says when a temporary’s object is dead and when its elements can be clobbered; a parameter’s reads are counted off the basic-block graph (local_live_after). No separate escape pass over the bytecode is needed.

4. Side exits and GC

A side exit while an object is pending performs the allocation in its write back: WriteBack::virtual_obj holds (dst, VirtualSrc) and runs last, after every other slot is homed, so the frame is GC-consistent across the allocating call (create_array over the element slots or the caller’s window, value_deep_copy of the template, or create_range from the endpoints). Both gen_write_back_for_deopt (x86-64) and a64_gen_write_back_for_deopt do this, and the chain-deopt conversion of a frame suspended in a call does the same for its handed-over objects.

At a GC safepoint the object’s slot is V, so the GC write back stores nil into it; the pinned element slots hold their (boxed, homed) values and are scanned like any frame slot. A handed-over object’s elements are in the caller’s frame, which the caller spilled before the call (write_back_range) and which is on the control-frame chain.

5. What is not covered

  • Locals. x = [a, b]; … x.max builds the Array: only a temporary (or a parameter handed one, §6) holds an elided object. The stage that kept objects in locals was removed in 2026-11 (see the introduction).
  • Block boundaries. An object is never carried into a merge or a loop head (§3), so a parameter’s object live past a branch, a guard clause or an optional parameter’s prologue is built at the end of the block.
  • Elements overwritten before the use. [a, b].include?(c + 1) evaluates c + 1 into the first element’s slot, so the object is materialized there. A local or literal argument (include?(x)) is passed in its own slot and does not clobber. The same happens to a literal followed by another argument: in size([i, 2], 1) the 1 is evaluated into the literal’s first element slot, so only a literal in the last positional position (or alone) reaches the callee elided; a literal of immediates (Literal) has no element slots and is not affected.
  • Slots objects and transparent callees. Without a template there is no Array to hand a transparent callee; only the elements lowerings apply. [a, b][i] and args[i] build the Array.
  • Return values. A specialized callee’s returned object is built at its ret, unless the call site discards the result (§8).
  • Hash literals and **kwrest. Both are built as they are written.
  • Range endpoints of unknown class. (a..b.size).sum builds the Range: the end is a call’s result, not proven Fixnum at the Range instruction. A Float, Bignum or String endpoint builds it too. The endpoint temporary of (a..f(b)).include?(x) is clobbered by the argument push, as an Array’s elements are.

6. Into callees: VirtualSrc::CallerSlots

A specialized callee (compile_specialized_func, LinkMode::from_caller) is compiled for one call site, with the caller’s abstract state at the call in hand. Two kinds of parameter can then start as an elided object:

  • the *rest parameter, over the caller’s argument window that the callee would bind into a new Array — def f(*args) = args.size, and the ... of a forwarding trampoline def f(...) = g(...);
  • a positional parameter whose argument is itself an elided literal in the caller — size([a, b]), t([1, 2], x).

Both are VirtualSrc::CallerSlots { src, len, base }, the caller’s slot window src..src+len read through the base the callee’s frame knows:

SlotBaseCalleeElement i lives at
SavedFpframed[[rbp] - rbp_local(src + i)]: the caller’s frame pointer, saved at [rbp] by the callee’s prologue
Window(delta)frameless (frameless_call.rs)[r14 + delta - conv(src + i)]: the callee runs in a window delta below the caller’s locals, so the caller’s slots are at a constant offset from its own LFP
Own—the frame’s own slot src + i: what a Slots object is, used by the shared lowerings only

A caller’s Literal object is handed over as it is (the template is global).

The hand-over (specialized_iseq): the caller decides handover = Some(base) when the call is specialized on its arguments and the callee passes the gate below; from_caller then returns, next to the parameter link modes, the objects to register at the callee’s entry (SlotState::new_method). The caller stores nil into the parameter’s slot in the callee frame instead of the value (fetch_arg_for_callee), skips create_array for the rest window, and spills the window (write_back_range) so that the callee’s reads and any side exit’s rebuild find the elements in memory. A literal inside the rest window is materialized first: it is an element there, not a parameter. The caller’s own entry for the object is taken at the end of the fill: the object now belongs to the callee.

The callee gate (caller_slots_ok): an iseq that cannot capture its locals without a block (possibly_capture_without_block: no binding, eval, local_variables, …), has no block literal, super or yield (ISeqInfo::forwarding_no_escape), and rescues nothing. Then a parameter whose reads are all behind it is dead for good, and nothing in the body can observe the slot except through the compiler. The gate reads the callee’s own iseq; a call it makes to a capturing method (binding, eval) resolves through the inline cache and counts as a read of every object of the frame in settle_virtuals (captures), so the parameter is materialized before the call.

Lifetime in the callee. A parameter’s object follows §3 with one difference: it survives the frame’s own calls, since its elements are not in this frame. It is materialized when read (a Mov, an argument to a non-specialized call, a ret, an index base), at the end of its basic block while still live, or when read by an instruction that cannot consume it; dropped when local_live_after says nothing reads it any more. It is not handed over again: a CallerSlots object passed to a further specialized callee is materialized, except for the forwarding consume below.

The forwarding consume. The rest of def f(...) = g(...) is consumed by the g(*rest, **kwrest, &blk) call itself: set_arguments’ forwarding arm reads the object (SetArgumentsForwarded::deferred_src) and copies the caller’s window straight into g’s frame, or builds g’s own *rest from the window’s tail (forwarded_deferred_layout), whenever g’s bind is a compile-time constant. The rest slot stays elided through the call (arg_forwarding_jit.md §3.4). The forwarding consume works on a generic call too — it is the only consume of a CallerSlots object that does not need the callee specialized — so settle_virtual_args leaves the trailing ... splat to it.

Reads that consume. ElementsOp lowerings over a CallerSlots object read the caller’s window: ArrayMinMax { base, args, len } for min / max, LoadCallerSlot { base, slot } for first / last, constants for size / empty?. Materialization is CreateArrayFrom { base, src, len } (runtime::create_array over the window); the same addressing is used by the side-exit write-back, by the chain-deopt replay stub of a frame suspended in a call (through [rsi] / [x24] for the saved bp, rdx / x25 for the window), and by the frameless callee’s exit write-back.

What it buys. def f(*args)-style helpers (args.size, args.first, args.last, args.max) and ... trampolines (Class#new’s forward to initialize included) run without the rest Array; literal arguments into def size(a) = a.size-style callees without the literal. The mechanism replaced the former deferred-rest annotation (D1): the kw half (K1) keeps its annotation (DeferredForward { kw }), the rest half is this.

7. Range literals: VirtualSrc::Range
